meaning.evidence: "He graduated from Wesleyan in 1869 and the Divinity School of Boston University in 1871" preserves the qualifications; dates, names, activities and quotations survive.

sense.evidence: "made no bones about his opposition" accurately conveys outspoken opposition.

authenticity.evidence: "got through", "going flat out" and "durries" are natural local usages.

register.evidence: "a fair bit of influence" and "never let up on" bring an Australian cadence, though some biographical linking remains relatively restrained for level 4.

tone.evidence: "After funeral services here tomorrow, his body will be sent" remains respectful, with no gag or disparaging aside.

flow.evidence: "Among a long list of titles that raise no eyebrows, one curious one stands out" cleanly retells a long original sentence.

variety.evidence: "made no bones", "going flat out" and "raise no eyebrows" offer variety without recurring tags.

essence.evidence: "He averaged six lectures a week, delivered in twenty-nine different countries" retains the obituary’s unusual productivity portrait and contrasting public reputation.

A.summary: Accurate and respectful, with smooth idiomatic prose and slightly restrained vernacular weight.

meaning.evidence: "well known right across the country" adds a specific national extent to widely known; the rest of the names, chronology and quotations are intact.

sense.evidence: "he wrote a fair bit on moral questions" weakens prolific to a merely moderate quantity.

authenticity.evidence: "Those on side with him" and "stayed put" sound natural rather than theatrical.

register.evidence: "The mob on the other side", "a big hand" and "barely got a rest" give sustained, broad level-4 prose without swearing.

tone.evidence: "has died of pneumonia in hospital here today, aged 73" is respectful; the conversational opposition description does not become ridicule.

flow.evidence: "On top of a steady stream of papers for religious magazines" links smoothly into the editorship detail.

variety.evidence: "a big hand", "stayed put" and "having a go" provide varied idiom.

essence.evidence: "His pen and his voice barely got a rest" preserves the industrious reformer portrait and the public-amusements contrast.

sense.evidence: "a fair whack of the credit" appropriately conveys influential involvement; "rein in" conveys restricting use.

authenticity.evidence: "got precious little rest" and "a stack" are natural local expressions.

register.evidence: "sheer hard yakka", "his dad's church" and "stayed from then on" give broad level-4 vocabulary and cadence.

tone.evidence: "had a red-hot go at stopping" adds a slightly boisterous edge to an otherwise respectful obituary.
